text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - Canary deploy failing for service runtime-worker in us-west1. Alerts: pod crashLoopBackOff x3, 5% error rate spike on hosted API text-generation. Paging eng-oncall.

mike: acked. I see canary pods immediately go CrashLoopBackOff with signal SIGILL on container start. Past deploy pushed a new multi-arch image tag. suspect arch mismatch.

aisha: any customer impact? @mike

mike: yes, hosted-api/us-west1 10% 500s for ~12m. Some Dedicated customers on west cluster reported intermittent 503s. No DB errors. No auth anomalies seen.

bryan: on it. Running `gcloud artifacts docker images list` then `crane digest` to verify. quick check:
```
$ crane digest us-docker.pkg.dev/redwood-registry/runtime:v20260315
sha256:abcdef1234567890...
$ crane manifest us-docker.pkg.dev/redwood-registry/runtime:v20260315 | jq .platforms
[ {"architecture":"amd64"}, {"architecture":"arm64"} ]
```
But canary nodes in the pool are `linux/arm64` only (autoscaler used arm instances), looks like image has amd64-only variant due to build failure earlier.

sara: how did the CI pick that tag? we pin tags by sha in prod. Does the pipeline push a 'v20260315' tag and also overwrite `latest`? @bryan

bryan: pipeline step `build-and-push` failed to produce multi-arch manifest for that build; but the subsequent `promote-to-canary` job didn't validate platforms. It promoted `v20260315-amd64` but named it `v20260315` in the registry accidentally (mutable tag got replaced).

mike: can we pause the rollout? We need the feature-flag kill-switch for canary traffic ASAP.

aisha: triggering kill-switch `deploy.canary.runtime-worker = false` now via console.

ops-bot: Feature flag change applied: `deploy.canary.runtime-worker=false` by aisha at 2026-03-15T02:00:12Z :white_check_mark:

mike: verified new pods aren't being created. Canary traffic cut. Errors dropping.

bryan: creating rollback to last good image sha. command:
```
kubectl -n runtime set image deploy/runtime-worker runtime-worker=us-docker.pkg.dev/redwood-registry/runtime@sha256:1234abcd
```
Executing now.

sara: watching. pods coming up healthy on arm64 nodes.

mike: hosted-api error rate back to baseline in us-west1. Confirmed with observability dashboard.

aisha: root cause: CI build produced an AMD-only image that was promoted without manifest validation. Missing multi-arch manifest + mutable tag policy allowed bad tag to replace multi-arch tag.

bryan: immediate mitigations:
- kill-switch applied to canary traffic
- rolled back canary to pinned sha
- added temporary admission webhook to block images without multi-arch manifest for `runtime-worker` in canary namespace

mike: next steps for dev/ci teams:
- fix `build-and-push` to always produce and verify manifest for all target platforms
- require promotion job to check `crane manifest` includes all platforms
- avoid using mutable tags for promotion (use immutable digests)

sara: customer comms: CS notified customers in affected region, said transient 500s for ~12m, no persisted data or credentials impacted. Ops to draft short postmortem.

aisha: handing off to night oncall @javier for follow-up and postmortem. summary saved to #incidents.

javier: acked, taking over. I'll validate the webhook and follow up with CI/infra tomorrow morning. Please ping if anything else pops up.

incident-bot: Incident closed (oncall resolved) 1799992134. Duration 900s. Severity downgraded to SEV3 after rollback.

mike: reaction :thumbsup:

sara: reaction :sparkles:
